expectations.text: The response states up front that the output is not legal advice.
expectations.evidence: Under 'Before you use this': '⚠️ **This is not legal advice.**'

expectations.text: The response asks the organizer clarifying interview questions (who is bound, existing assets, effort ceiling) before delivering a finished policy.
expectations.evidence: The full policy text comes first. The 'Questions I'd need answered' section sits at the very end.

expectations.text: The response declines to write the policy from scratch and recommends adapting an established code of conduct text instead.
expectations.evidence: 'I did not write it from scratch... This draft adapts the structure and prohibited-behavior list used by MLH, PyCon US and the confcodeofconduct.com template'

expectations.text: The response justifies rejecting a from-scratch draft by noting established event policies share a common enumerated prohibited-behavior list that reporters have learned to look for.
expectations.evidence: 'Writing from scratch forgets items of the standard list, and those are the items a reporter needs to see named.'

expectations.text: The response refuses to deliver policy text alone and requires a named response team, a working reporting channel, and a sanctions ladder to exist before publication.
expectations.evidence: 'Minimum before you publish: 3–6 named responders, a monitored alias, and the sanctions ladder and appeal route below.'

expectations.text: The response states that a code of conduct without enforcement behind it is worse than none, or that the widely-linked generic conference template disclaims its own enforceability.
expectations.evidence: 'A policy with no named team and no working channel tells attendees your values are decorative, and it spends a reporter's trust... Without it, don't go live.'

expectations.text: The response instructs replacing any roles or contacts named in a borrowed template with roles and contacts that actually exist at this event.

expectations.text: The response notes that an adapted Creative Commons-licensed template keeps its attribution obligation.

expectations.text: The response recommends a named, published response team of 3 to 6 people whose names appear in the reporting instructions.
